headline: South Korea's army showed a drill in which drones, robots and unmanned vehicles led the way, part of a plan to reorganise all its units around human-machine teams by 2040.
score_reason: Machines clearly shown in action in a demonstration, but it is a drill and a long-term plan.
importance_line: South Korean soldiers and conscripts are affected as machines take on the most dangerous jobs, but the 2040 goal is a plan and the drill was staged for the media.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports that the South Korean Army showed its Army TIGER+ exercise to the media on 14 Oct 2026, in which drones, unmanned vehicles and four-legged robots cleared a simulated minefield ahead of troops. The Army plans to organise all units into human-machine teams by 2040 because it has fewer conscripts.
notes: Demonstration, not combat. Military story: counts toward the robot-war limit.
